claims.statement: None of the deep learning models (GEARS, scGPT, UCE, scBERT, Geneformer) consistently outperformed the mean baseline or the linear model in predicting unseen single perturbation effects.

conditions: Prediction of expression changes after double perturbations using data from Norman et al., with 100 single-gene and 124 double-gene CRISPR activation perturbations in K562 cells. Models were fine-tuned on all 100 single and 62 double perturbations and tested on the remaining 62 double perturbations, repeated across 5 random train-test splits.
claims.statement: None of the seven deep learning models (scGPT, scFoundation, UCE, scBERT, Geneformer, GEARS, CPA) outperformed the additive baseline in predicting double perturbation effects; none outperformed the no-change baseline in predicting genetic interactions.

evidence_spans.text: Using the full dataset, we identified 5,035 genetic interactions (out of potentially 124,000) at a false discovery rate of 5%.
None of the models was better than the ‘no change’ baseline. The same ranking of models was observed when using other metrics (Extended Data Fig. 4).

The linear models with the gene embeddings from scFoundation and scGPT outperformed the ‘mean’ baseline, but they did not consistently outperform the linear model using G and P from the training data. The approach that did consistently outperform all other models was a linear model with P pretrained on the Replogle data (using the K562 cell line data as pretraining for the Adamson and RPE1 data and the RPE1 cell line for the K562 data).
To our surprise, we often found the same pair of hemoglobin genes (HBG2 and HBZ) among the top predicted interactions, across models and double perturbations (Extended Data Fig. 5).
None of the deep learning models was able to consistently outperform the mean prediction or the linear model (Fig. 2a and Extended Data Fig. 8).

limitations.statement: Only four datasets were used, all from cancer cell lines.
The benchmark tested only prediction of transcriptome changes after single or double perturbations; other tasks may yield different results.
Datasets are from cancer cell lines, which may have high mutational burden; some foundation models (e.g., Geneformer) excluded such data from training.
scFoundation was not included in single perturbation benchmark because most required genes were missing from Adamson and Replogle datasets.
Original quality control procedures were not improved; perturbations that did not affect expression of their own target gene were not excluded.
CPA was not evaluated in single perturbation benchmark as it is not designed for unseen perturbations.

methods.description: Represents each read-out gene with a K-dimensional vector (gene embedding G) and each perturbation with an L-dimensional vector (perturbation embedding P). G and P are derived via PCA from training data or from pretrained embeddings. W is found via ridge regression (λ=0.1). Predicts as Y_hat = G W P^T + b, where b is the row mean of training data.
